chief_complaint: Surveillance and management of stage 1 non‑small cell lung cancer with associated respiratory symptoms and comorbid hypertension, obesity, and prediabetes.
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 48‑year‑old male with a longstanding diagnosis of stage 1 non‑small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) first identified in 1967. He has been undergoing platinum‑taxane chemotherapy (cisplatin and paclitaxel) and serial thoracic CT imaging for disease surveillance. Recent active issues include acute bronchitis and viral sinusitis, for which he is taking acetaminophen and inhaled bronchodilators. Hypertension is well controlled on lisinopril and amlodipine, though diastolic pressure is low‑normal. He has obesity (BMI ≥30) and pre‑diabetes (A1c 6.3%). Chronic anemia is present. Psychosocial stressors are prominent, including social isolation, limited contact, and a history of intimate partner abuse. The visit pattern shows high inpatient and emergency utilization, reflecting frequent acute events and cancer‑related care.

past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include prior viral sinusitis, acute viral pharyngitis, leaking dental filling, and gingivitis. The patient has a history of childhood asthma (inferred from inhaled therapy), military service, higher education, and prior part‑time/full‑time employment. No chronic renal, hepatic, or cardiac disease beyond hypertension is documented.
